title: Alert against incidents of 'Blackmail' and 'Digital Arrest' by Cyber Criminals Impersonating State/UT Police, NCB, CBI, RBI and other Law Enforcement Agencies
publisher: Ministry of Home Affairs via Press Information Bureau
notes: MHA says fraudsters posing as Police, CBI, Narcotics, RBI and ED call victims about a parcel with drugs, fake passports or contraband, or claim a relative is in custody, and demand money to settle the 'case'. Victims are kept visible on Skype/video calls ('Digital Arrest') until they pay; fraudsters use studios made to look like police stations and wear uniforms. I4C blocked over 1,000 Skype IDs; report to 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in. (Opened via HTTP fetch of the PIB page; WebFetch returned 403.)

title: Steps taken to address the issue of digital arrest scams (Rajya Sabha written reply)
publisher: Ministry of Home Affairs via Press Information Bureau
notes: MoS Home Bandi Sanjay Kumar told Rajya Sabha that NCRB does not keep separate digital-arrest data; I4C had blocked more than 3,962 Skype IDs and 83,668 WhatsApp accounts used for digital arrest, and over 7.81 lakh SIMs and 2,08,469 IMEIs were blocked till 28.02.2025. The Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting system had saved over Rs 4,386 crore in 13.36 lakh+ complaints; awareness includes the PM's Mann Ki Baat of 27.10.2024 and 1930 caller tunes. (Opened via HTTP fetch; WebFetch returned 403.)

title: PM's address in the 115th Episode of 'Mann Ki Baat'
notes: PM describes digital-arrest callers posing as Police, CBI, Narcotics or RBI, who first collect personal details, then create fear with uniforms and office set-ups, then apply time pressure ('decide now or be arrested'). States no agency inquires or demands money by phone/video call and that there is no system like digital arrest in law; advises 'Stop - Think - Take Action', call 1930, report on cybercrime.gov.in, inform family and police.

title: Digital arrests and cyber crimes under watch: over 7.81 lakh SIM cards blocked by Feb
notes: Reports MoS Home Bandi Sanjay Kumar's written reply: digital arrest cases were 39,925 (Rs 91.14 crore) in 2022, 60,676 (Rs 339.03 crore) in 2023, 1,23,672 (Rs 1935.51 crore) in 2024 and 17,718 (Rs 210.21 crore) in 2025 up to 28 Feb.

title: Will deal with iron hand: top court on Rs 3,000 cr extortion via digital arrests
notes: Supreme Court bench (Justice Surya Kant) in its suo motu case said about Rs 3,000 crore had been extorted from victims including senior citizens. Triggered by an Ambala couple (73-year-old woman) defrauded of over Rs 1.05 crore using forged court, ED and PMLA orders with stamps and seals, over audio/video calls with fake CBI/ED/judicial officers.

title: CBI, ED, Police Don't Arrest People Through Video Calls: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre
notes: Reports an I4C public advisory (5 Oct 2024): CBI, police, customs, ED and judges do not arrest people on video calls. Fraudsters claim the target or a family member is caught in drugs or money laundering, confine them with cameras on, and demand online 'bail' money; report to 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in.

title: SBI Hyderabad saves senior citizen from Rs 13 lakh scam
notes: A 61-year-old doctor under 'digital arrest' came to an SBI branch to break FDs, telling staff it was to buy property; his vague answers raised suspicion. Fraudsters kept him on the phone during branch visits; staff delayed the transaction, asked him to bring a family member, and connected him to 1930.

title: Telangana vigilance secretary cautions public against digital arrest
notes: Telangana Vigilance secretary Shikha Goel says fake police callers tell victims to isolate themselves and not inform anyone, then ask them to move money to (mule) accounts for 'verification' with a promise it will be returned. She states digital arrest is not a legal process.

title: FedEx scam: Bengaluru software engineer loses Rs 1 crore to fraudsters
notes: A fake FedEx executive said a Taiwan-bound parcel in her name held narcotics and passports at Mumbai airport; fake customs and Mumbai Police took over on Skype, told her to stay in an isolated room with camera on, and had her pay about Rs 1 crore to an 'RBI' account for verification, promising refund within 30 days. FedEx says it does not seek personal information over calls; police note law enforcement does not use Skype.

title: FedEx courier scam: A tale of terror, trickery, and deceit
notes: Only the standfirst was readable (body gated): data accessed by DH showed 111 FedEx courier scam cases registered up to November 2023, a scam that came to the fore that year (jurisdiction of the count not visible in the standfirst; DH is Bengaluru-based).

title: Govt debunks SMS from India Post asking people to update their address
notes: PIB Fact Check labelled as fake an SMS claiming to be from India Post asking recipients to update their address; India Post does not send such messages for delivery, and people should not click the links.

title: Centre issues Advisory Against Mobile Calls Impersonating DoT
publisher: ETV Bharat (reporting Department of Telecommunications advisory)
notes: DoT warned of callers in its name threatening that all the citizen's mobile numbers will be disconnected or are being misused in illegal activities, and of WhatsApp calls from foreign numbers (e.g. +92) impersonating officials. DoT authorises no one to make such calls; report on Chakshu (Sanchar Saathi), check connections via 'Know Your Mobile Connections', and call 1930 if defrauded.

title: TRAI issues advisory on frauds misusing TRAI's identity
publisher: SCC Online Blog (reporting TRAI advisory of 6 Aug 2025)
notes: TRAI says it does not investigate consumers, ask for Aadhaar/bank details/OTP, threaten arrest, or initiate contact about number disconnection, and authorises no third party to do so. Fraudsters impersonating TRAI use forged documents, KYC-disconnection threats, digital-arrest tactics, demands for bail/fines/'verification', and fake high-rent mobile tower offers with upfront fees and forged TRAI letters.

title: Your Number Will Be Blocked in 2 Hours, Press 9: New Scam Alert! TRAI Issues Warning
notes: Describes an IVR call saying the number will be blocked within two hours and to press 9; a fake TRAI official then says another SIM in the victim's name sent harassing messages, cites a fake FIR, and pushes a police 'clarification', sometimes transferring to fake police. TRAI says it does not call to block numbers.

title: India reports 31 lakh complaints against spam calls and digital arrest scams in 2025; 33,000 numbers blocked
notes: Citing TRAI data: spam-call complaints were 13.62 lakh (2023), 19.38 lakh (2024) and 31.09 lakh (2025), and telcos blocked about 33,000 numbers. Advises victims to tell their bank and mobile provider immediately and report on 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in / Chakshu.

title: Duped of Rs 5 lakhs, retired air force personnel becomes victim of 'digital arrest' in Faridabad
notes: Standfirst read (body gated): scammers demanded the victim's bank details and kept him under 'digital arrest', warning him not to disconnect the video call or they would act against his family. Search snippet of the same report: it began with a fake TRAI caller saying his number would be deactivated in two hours over a SIM obtained with his Aadhaar, followed by a fake CBI officer.

title: RBI cautions against frauds in the name of KYC updation (Press Release 2023-2024/1794)
notes: RBI repeats its 13 Sep 2021 caution: fraudsters send unsolicited calls/SMS/emails to extract personal or login details or get customers to install unverified apps via links, creating false urgency by threatening account freezing/blocking/closure. Advises contacting the bank directly using numbers from its official website, never sharing credentials/OTP/KYC copies, and reporting to cybercrime.gov.in or 1930. (Opened via HTTP fetch; WebFetch hit a bot check.)

title: BE(A)WARE - A booklet on Modus Operandi of Financial Fraudsters
publisher: Reserve Bank of India (Office of RBI Ombudsman)
notes: RBI booklet compiled from Ombudsman complaints. Vishing: impostors pose as bankers, insurance agents or government officials, quote a few personal details, and cite urgency (block an unauthorised transaction, stop a penalty) to get OTP/PIN/CVV. Search-engine fraud: fake customer-care numbers for banks, insurers or Aadhaar centres are planted in search results; customer care numbers are never mobile numbers. Also covers SIM swap via fake 3G-to-4G upgrade offers. (rbidocs mirror blocked by bot check; read the rbi.org.in commonman copy.)

title: Raju and the Forty Thieves - pictorial booklet on fraud modus operandi
publisher: Reserve Bank of India (Office of RBI Ombudsman Mumbai-II and CEPD); copy hosted by a bank at scc.bank.in
notes: RBI pictorial booklet of forty fraud stories reported to RBI Ombudsmen/CEPD; only the foreword, index and a few captions are machine-readable. Story titles include KYC phishing link followed by a call and a Rs 50,000 debit, credit card annual fee waiver fake offer, credit card activation fraud, credit card limit upgradation fraud, social welfare scheme fraud, safeguarding your Aadhaar card, and fraud by compromising credentials through search engines.

title: PIB flags fake SBI YONO message urging Aadhaar update, warns customers against phishing scam
notes: PIB Fact Check flagged messages claiming SBI YONO accounts would be blocked over incomplete Aadhaar details unless users installed a KYC-named APK. SBI confirmed it does not ask customers to download APK files for Aadhaar updates; PIB advised not to install apps or APKs sent via email, SMS or WhatsApp.

title: Message from SBI to update your PAN card details is a scam, do not fall for it
notes: PIB Fact Check called fake an SMS in SBI's name saying the YONO account was closed and asking the customer to update PAN via a link to avoid blocking. SBI never asks for personal details by message; report to report.phishing@sbi.co.in or 1930.

title: Fact Check: Maharashtra DGIPR Warns Of Fake Electricity Bill Messages, Urges Citizens To Stay Alert
notes: Maharashtra DGIPR and MSEDCL warn of messages threatening power cuts over pending bills and asking consumers to call a personal mobile number. MSEDCL never contacts consumers from personal numbers, uses authorised sender IDs such as VM-MSEDCL, and never asks consumers to download third-party apps; helplines 1912 / 1800-212-3435 / 1800-233-3435.

title: Sr citizen loses Rs 1.2L in electricity bill scam
notes: A 66-year-old retired officer got a WhatsApp message that power would be cut at 9:30 pm over an unpaid bill; the fake 'electricity officer' asked him to pay Rs 100 and install 'Quick support', after which Rs 49,000 and Rs 50,000 were debited. PSPCL says it never sends SMS/WhatsApp messages about pending bills.

title: Telangana electricity board warns people against online fraud
date: on or before 5 Aug 2023 (last modified date)
notes: TSSPDCL cautions about texts saying power will be cut at 9:30 pm because last month's bill was not updated, asking consumers to call an 'electricity officer' who gets them to install Quick Support/AnyDesk and then takes banking and card details. TSSPDCL does not send payment links; pay only via its app or website; call 1930.

title: Fake e-challan SMS scam: Kerala Police caution against malicious APKs
notes: Kerala Police warn of SMS from private numbers with realistic e-challan details and a link to a cloned MVD e-challan portal that asks for the vehicle number, shows a fake security check and downloads a malicious APK. Genuine e-challan services never require APK downloads; check only on official MVD/Parivahan portals and report to 1930.

title: Vietnamese hackers fuelling WhatsApp e-challan scam in India: Report
notes: Reports CloudSEK research: WhatsApp messages impersonating Parivahan Sewa or Karnataka Police deliver a Wromba-family APK that seizes SMS (OTP interception), harvests contacts to spread, and is used to buy and redeem gift cards. Over 4,400 devices infected; one operator's fraud exceeded Rs 16 lakh (271 gift cards, Rs 16,31,000); Gujarat and Karnataka most affected.

title: SCAM ALERT! Don't Fall for Fake Income Tax Emails (e-Filing portal home-page banner)
publisher: Income Tax Department, Government of India (incometax.gov.in)
notes: Banner on the official e-Filing home page states that official Income Tax Department communications never contain hyperlinks; any such email should be treated as fraudulent and not clicked, and all services should be accessed via incometax.gov.in.

title: Fraud Alert: From e-Challan, Gas Bill Updates to APK Traps - How Malware Scams Are Draining Bank Accounts
notes: Describes APK campaigns (e.g. 'MParivahan.apk' with a hidden second app overlaying fake banking screens; CERT-In alerted on it) and fake LPG messages saying a booking needs renewal or KYC update to keep cylinder deliveries during a shortage, leading to fake booking/payment pages and 'Gas Bill Update.apk'. Also lists fake income-tax refund alerts leading to phishing sites that capture net-banking passwords; advises using only official OMC apps/portals.

title: A validated bank account is necessary for credit of refunds (e-Filing portal home-page banner)
publisher: Income Tax Department, Government of India (incometax.gov.in)
notes: Official banner: refunds are credited only to a validated bank account, which the taxpayer validates by logging in to incometax.gov.in > My Profile > My Bank Account and e-verifying.

title: Fraud Alert: That 'IMP' message from the Income-Tax Department could be a trap
notes: Catalogues fake I-T emails: 'Important Message' notices with fake ITBA reference numbers linking off-portal, fake penalty/prosecution notices with 72-hour deadlines, fake demand notices (PIB flagged an AY25-26 demand and a Rs 6,000 demand as phishing), a Rs 60,000 refund 'manual verification' email PIB flagged as credential theft, and fake e-PAN downloads; CloudSEK reported WhatsApp/email penalty notices delivering OTP-stealing malware. The department never asks for PINs, passwords or OTPs by email/SMS.

title: Fraud Alert: Govt Schemes Scam
notes: Lists PIB Fact Check-flagged scheme hoaxes: free 'Students' Laptop Scheme 2025' phishing, free recharge, free solar flour mill for rural women requiring Aadhaar and a small registration fee, forged government loan approval letters of Rs 3 lakh demanding a Rs 36,500 'legal insurance charge' (Finance Ministry denied), and fake HPCL/OMC LPG dealership letters (applications only via lpgvitarakchayan.in). Advises never paying registration/processing fees and verifying on .gov.in sites.

title: Fraud Alert: Beware of bogus websites offering govt schemes, loan on phone
notes: MNRE warned of fake PM-KUSUM (farmer solar pump) portals that rank high in search results; callers quoted Rs 51,000 for a pump and took a Rs 5,600 'registration' payment with a promised refund. Also a Thane loan-on-phone case where fake bank officials demanded processing charges (Rs 7.34 lakh recovered). Verify schemes via official ministry portals or india.gov.in.

title: Fraud Alert: Why Seniors Are in the Crosshairs
notes: Documents senior-citizen losses (e.g. an 82-year-old Delhi man lost Rs 22.92 crore to digital arrest; a 77-year-old Mumbai man paid over Rs 2.25 crore after a fake terror-funding accusation). Victims are told to stay under 'digital custody', not speak to family and not leave home; some refuse to listen to bank staff who flag transfers. Reports that in Nagpur 60% of 2025 cyber-fraud victims were seniors (Rs 45.77 crore lost); suggests a family rule of one call before any large transfer.

title: Fraud Alert: Twitter verification mail; beware of calls for updating life certificate
notes: Fraudsters posing as the pension department call pensioners during the November life-certificate season, quoting PPO number, retirement date, Aadhaar and nominee details, and ask for an OTP 'to update the life certificate', then empty the account. CPAO warned pensioners not to respond; life certificates can be given at the bank or via the Aadhaar-based Jeevan Pramaan portal.

title: Attention Pensioners (home-page notice on cyber fraud calls about Life Certificate)
publisher: Central Pension Accounting Office, Ministry of Finance
notes: CPAO home page warns that cyber fraudsters are calling pensioners about updating their Life Certificate online and asking for personal details and OTPs; CPAO states it does not call for Life Certificate submission or ask for personal information.

title: EPFO Urges Members to Avoid Approaching Unauthorized Agents and Use Official EPFO Portals for Free & Secure Online Services
publisher: Ministry of Labour & Employment via PIB (copy hosted on EPFO CDN)
notes: EPFO says cyber-cafe operators and fintech firms are charging members large sums for services that are free, which also exposes members' financial data; all EPFO services (claims, transfers, KYC, grievances) are entirely free and members should not pay third-party agents. Auto-settlement of advance claims was raised to Rs 1 lakh (2.34 crore auto claims in FY 2024-25). PIB Release ID 2136592.

title: Ministry of Labour & Employment Cautions Citizens Against Fake PMVBRY Portals
publisher: Ministry of Labour & Employment via PIB (copy hosted on EPFO CDN)
notes: Ministry disowns websites such as viksitbharatrozgaryojana.org and pmviksitbharatrozgaryojana.com that falsely claim to recruit under the PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana; citizens should not share personal information or make payments on such portals; genuine portal is pmvbry.epfindia.gov.in / pmvbry.labour.gov.in. PIB Release ID 2163332.

title: Fraud Alert: Insurance maturity bonus; pay-by-QR code scam
notes: Delhi Police arrested a 32-year-old who, posing as an RBI deputy general manager, told an 82-year-old retired professor his insurance policies had matured with a Rs 90 lakh bonus, demanded a Rs 1.5 lakh processing fee and kept asking for more until the victim had paid Rs 90 lakh (from 2018). Advises verifying directly with the insurer.

title: Fraud Alert: SBI interest certificates and Mahanagar Gas disconnection
notes: WhatsApp messages with Mahanagar Gas logo say supply will be cut tonight at 9:30 pm unless the bill is updated; callers seek a Rs 10 'system update' fee or Rs 1,150 payment, then push 'BILL_UPDATE.apk' and capture banking credentials (one Mumbai man lost about Rs 11.82 lakh). More than 130 MGL customers reportedly targeted since late March with about Rs 3 crore lost; MGL says it never asks for OTPs, bank details or passwords. Also covers fake SBI WhatsApp 'interest certificate' messages.

title: Fraud Alert: Fake credit card offers, malicious files and new guaranteed income scams
notes: A Facebook 'bank' ad for a lounge-access credit card led to a caller posing as a bank representative who sent a WhatsApp 'form' that was an APK; it captured messages and OTPs and two unauthorised transactions of nearly Rs 50,000 each hit the victim's other cards. Notes genuine bank calls come from 1600-series numbers and bank emails from .bank.in.

title: Caution Against Fraudulent/Unauthorised Website Impersonating IRDAI Bima Bharosa/IGMS (Public Notice IRDAI/PPGR/BB/2026-27/25)
publisher: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
notes: IRDAI says igmsirdai.online and irdaiigms.com are not official; the public should not submit personal, policy, banking, KYC or OTP details, or make any payment through such sites, should register insurance complaints only at bimabharosa.irdai.gov.in, and should be cautious of websites, emails, messages or phone calls misusing IRDAI's name or logo.

title: Fraud Alert: Payment link scam; be careful of SMS forwarding apps
notes: Reports CloudSEK findings of phishing sites posing as bank complaint portals: a caller posing as a bank executive sends the link and asks for card number, CVV and expiry to issue a 'refund' for a 'failed transaction', then gets an SMS-forwarding app installed to capture OTPs. A traveller who complained about a booking on social media got a fake HDFC call pushing a survey link and an SMS-forwarding app. Advises never searching online for customer-care numbers.

title: Fraud Alert: Fake banking apps, cheater e-commerce websites
notes: Delhi Police arrested 23 people in a pan-India network that sent bulk SMS links to fake SBI YONO pages (and in one case a fake KYC-update app), captured credentials, took over accounts and moved money to mule accounts; police found more than 100 such cases, with modules spanning Jamtara, Surat, Kolkata and Delhi NCR.

title: Security - Protect your Card (Types of Frauds)
notes: Issuer's fraud page describes malicious APK files shared via SMS/email/WhatsApp, impersonation of government agencies to get card details, account takeover through shared OTPs (followed by mobile/email change and cross-sell bookings), and screen-sharing fraud where callers posing as the bank have users type card details; states SBI Card will never ask customers to install any third-party application.

title: RBI cautions Public Once Again against Fictitious Offers
notes: RBI states it never contacts the public by unsolicited calls or emails asking for money or personal information, does not hold accounts for individuals or give money to individuals, and warns of people impersonating RBI officials who demand processing fees, tax clearance or conversion charges into specified accounts, followed by escalating demands. (Opened via HTTP fetch.)

title: Fraud Alert: True stories about how people are being cheated everyday
notes: Includes an Andheri businessman who lost Rs 21.17 lakh after responding to a 'Rs 1 international credit card' offer, sharing personal details and approving a Rs 1 transfer through a link; also a fake lottery letter (Rs 11.5 lakh lost over 14 transfers) and Tripura electricity-disconnection SMS warnings.

title: Public Notice: Beware of fraud in the name of TRAI (mobile tower leasing) F. No. 812-4/2012-TD
notes: TRAI notice (linked from its consumer-protection page) says companies/agencies/individuals ask the public to deposit money as 'Government Tax under Telecom Act' for leasing premises for mobile towers, issue fake NOCs purportedly from the Ministry of Communications and IT, and become unreachable after collecting money; TRAI is not involved in any tax/fee on tower leasing or in issuing such NOCs. (Image-only PDF read visually.)

title: Fraud Alert: Beware of Aadhaar-enabled Payment System frauds and fake apps
notes: Notes the national cybercrime portal warned of AePS fraud that needs no OTP and advises locking biometrics on the UIDAI website/Aadhaar app; describes a senior citizen whose money was withdrawn via a banking correspondent from an account she never used, Delhi Police findings of silicone fingerprints used to access UIDAI systems, and Telangana police advice to disable Aadhaar biometric linking after AePS fraud.

title: Fraud Alert: Beware of electricity bill scam; Rs14.64 lakh withdrawn using Aadhaar fingerprints
notes: Cyberabad police busted a seven-member gang that downloaded property registration documents from the Andhra Pradesh IGRS website, made polymer fingerprints and used an AePS business-correspondent licence to withdraw Rs 14.64 lakh from 149 customers; police said over 10,000 fake fingerprints were prepared and 2,500 cloned prints were seized.

title: National Scholarship Portal home page announcements
notes: Official NSP announcements: applications for 2026-27 are made on the portal (open from 1 June 2026, student deadline 31 Oct 2026 for listed schemes); NSP services are also available at Common Service Centres, where the total charge for the entire activity per candidate (reference number, biometric authentication, OTR and full application) is fixed at Rs 30 inclusive of taxes. No fraud warning was found on the page.

title: Fraud Alert: Beware of these 5 SMS, calls
notes: Covers a fake HDFC Bank PAN-update SMS with a short link, WhatsApp free-gift links, and an electricity-bill SMS where UP's chief forest conservator was asked to call a number, install AnyDesk and transfer Re 1, then lost about Rs 1.23 lakh (per IANS). Notes nobody offers bumper returns, bonuses or insurance payouts over the phone.

title: Fraud Alert: Money extortion scam in the name of customs; beware of fake notices from I4C
notes: Fraudsters posing as Indian Customs (or as social-media/matrimonial contacts 'detained' with a costly gift) demand customs duty into personal bank accounts; PIB says Customs never calls or SMSes asking for duty in personal accounts and genuine communications carry a DIN verifiable on the CBIC site. Also fake emails in the name of the I4C CEO alleging a court order for visiting illegal sites with 24-48 hour deadlines; PIB Fact Check and Cyberdost called them fake.

title: Fraud Alert: Beware, fake emails on tax, criminal action are increasing
notes: Describes a fake email (signed as GST department) telling a taxpayer her tax payment was frozen and asking her to pay a challan via a link, tax phishing peaking around filing/refund season (Income Tax India warned on X on 21 Jul 2024), and a recurring fake 'Office of the Commissioner of Police' email accusing a student of an offence involving minors, with a PDF bearing CBI/IB/cyber-cell logos and fake stamps demanding a reply.
